AlternateTargets: the one great matter and occasion

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Chan records inherit “the single great matter” as the reason for a buddha's appearance, then turn it into a live question whose answers can point to seeing one's nature, opening a hall, daily scenery, or the acts of a case.
EvidenceBody: Yuanwu Keqin says buddhas appear for the single great matter and links Bodhidharma's coming with seeing one's nature. The Jingde Lamp Record preserves a reviewed unnamed monastic questioner asking Touzi Datong what the single great matter is; Touzi answers that Yin Sikong has opened the hall for him. Tianyin Yuanxiu reviews that answer beside Yuanwu's alternative and says the older teachers' presentations have no superiority or inferiority.

Juelang Daosheng and Guxue Zhe repeat the appearance formula in direct instruction, the latter calling buddhas and ancestral teachers lamps for the world. Ruibai Mingxue identifies the matter with opening, showing, awakening to, and entering buddha-knowledge, and maps a flower held up and Kasyapa's smile onto that sequence. Jie'an Wujin quotes the appearance formula and immediately raises his staff, treating the inherited phrase as an occasion for present showing rather than a detachable definition.

Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support one inherited formula with varied Chan deployment; “single great matter” is the established lookup form, while “reason and occasion” (因緣) remains explicit here.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: An inherited reason-for-appearance formula becomes a question answered through the very occasion at hand: an opening hall, natural scene, staff gesture, or cited case.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: Touzi's opening-hall answer and the later plurality of answers prevent treating “reason and occasion” (因緣) as one abstract definition detachable from its occasion.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All explicitly cite or answer the same single-great-matter formula while varying its present enactment.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases preserve the established one-great-matter lookup and add purpose and appearance routes for constructions using “reason and occasion” (因緣).

ModifierControls.Finding: “One” (一) scopes “great matter” (大事), while “reason and occasion” (因緣) supplies the appearance construction rather than a second independent sense.

FamilyControls.Finding: Common shortened form, related but not substituted into exact evidence.
Ruibai's explicit unpacking of the inherited appearance formula, not imposed as the wording of every answer.
